issue_title: register storage class specifier causes -Wregister warnings when compiled as C++17 (stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h, stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h)
clean_text:
Title: register storage class specifier causes -Wregister warnings when compiled as C++17 (stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h, stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h)

Body:
Caution
The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project.
For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post a topic in the [ST Community/STM32 MCUs forum](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)

Describe the set-up

Custom board using STM32C011F6Px
GNU Tools for STM32 (13.3.rel1) — arm-none-eabi-g++ with -std=gnu++17
Describe the bug
Eight uses of the register storage class specifier remain in the LL driver headers. The register keyword is deprecated in C++11 and removed in C++17; any project compiled with -std=c++17 or -std=gnu++17 receives a warning (treated as an error with -Werror):

Affected locations:
Drivers/STM32C0xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h 
line 4010, 4115, 4120

Drivers/STM32C0xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h
line 1077, 1105, 1410, 1438, 1741

How To Reproduce

Create any C++ project targeting STM32C0 that includes stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h or stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h and calls the affected LL functions.
Compile with -std=c++17 (or -std=gnu++17).
The compiler emits [-Wregister] warnings for each of the eight lines listed above.

Additional context
The fix is straightforward — remove the register keyword from the eight variable declarations. The qualifier has had no effect on code generation in modern compilers for many years.

issue_title: I2C Master Memory Read function actually sends a write command
clean_text:
Title: I2C Master Memory Read function actually sends a write command

Body:
**Hardware**
Exact processor: STM32C092CCU6 on a custom PCB
Interfacing with TLE493DW2B6A1HTSA1 hall magnetic vector sensor

**Describe the bug**
section 2.1.3.1 of the Infineon user manual for this sensor shows a timing diagram in Figure 7. The master is required to send the 7-bit device address, followed by a read bit (value 1) for the first byte, then 8 more control bits including the register address to be read. Function HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_IT in stm32c0xx_hal_i2c.c line 2945 calls I2C_TransferConfig with the final parameter I2C_GENERATE_START_WRITE which causes the 7-bit address to be followed by a write bit (value 0) instead.

It is my understanding, the purpose of HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_IT  is to allow the processor to control the SDA line for 2 or 3 bytes before releasing control for the slave to take over, which makes it ideal for the 2-byte read mode in this sensor. I have changed I2C_GENERATE_START_WRITE as referenced above to I2C_GENERATE_START_READ, and the bug goes away. I was further able to see that register bit I2Cx->CR2->RD_WRN was not set before my fix, and was set after my fix.

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2025-09-03T14:51:05Z]
Hello @AndrewWern,

Thank you for the report.

Regarding the issue, and after a first analysis, the API HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_IT() is used to read data from a specific memory address. The first step after the start condition is to write the memory address (send the slave address with the write bit (value 0 as you mentioned), then configure the memory address size usually 1 or2 bytes. The 4th parameter indicates the Reload End mode used which is I2C_SOFTEND_MODE "this prevent automatic STOP generation after sending the memory address and allows the driver to generate a repeated START later for the read phase". This is why we have the I2C_GENERATE_START_WRITE request in the I2C_TransferConfig() function, after all these steps, the slave responds by sending the requested data bytes. The Read phase it happens inside the I2C_Mem_ISR_IT() interrupt subroutine which is configured on line 2923.

For the bit I2Cx->CR2->RD_WRN, and based on the RM0490 Rev5, it's indicated the Transfer direction (controller mode). It is normal for the bit to be 1 when the I2C_GENERATE_START_READ request is configured.

This may be a particular case for this sensor, could you please share the Infineon user manual (I couldn't find it), in order to share it
with our team, as well as a snippet of code for further analysis.

With regards,

Title: Error in stm32c0xx_hal_spi

Body:
While using the STM32C0 HAL library, I noticed an error in the stm32c0xx_hal_spi.c file. During 8-bit data transmission, the driver uses uint16_t to read the register, which results in incorrect data copying. I believe this should be corrected to uint8_t.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16114acf-1108-4371-9e50-846a733f651e)

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2025-06-30T15:10:17Z]
Hello @hhq-123,

Thank you for the report.

Regarding the issue and after a first analysis, please take a look at the brief section in the file stm32c0xx_hal_spi.c from line 71, which mentions:

> Data buffer address alignment restriction:
      (#) In case more than 1 byte is requested to be transferred, the HAL SPI uses 16-bit access for data buffer.
          But there is no support for unaligned accesses on the Cortex-M0 processor.
          So, if the user wants to transfer more than 1 byte, it shall ensure that 16-bit aligned address is used for:
          (##) pData parameter in HAL_SPI_Transmit(), HAL_SPI_Transmit_IT(), HAL_SPI_Receive() and HAL_SPI_Receive_IT()
          (##) pTxData and pRxData parameters in HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive() and HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_IT()
      (#) There is no such restriction when going through DMA by using HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA(), HAL_SPI_Receive_DMA()
          and HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_DMA().

Also, in case of transmitting data in 8-bit mode, the driver supports packing mode.

  c   if (hspi->TxXferCount > 1U)
      {
        /* write on the data register in packing mode */
        hspi->Instance->DR = *((const uint16_t *)hspi->pTxBuffPtr);

 Otherwise, could you share more details about the error, your project and the SPI config for further analysis.

With regards,

[KRASTM - 2025-07-21T08:27:00Z]
Hello @hhq-123,

Please, allow me to close the issue, thank you in advance for your understanding.

With regards,

issue_title: IAR STM32C0 patch : Failed to load flash loader FlashSTM32C03xx6.flash
clean_text:
Title: IAR STM32C0 patch : Failed to load flash loader FlashSTM32C03xx6.flash

Body:
Hello,

I am using IAR EW 8.32 for a development project using an STM32C031C6 nucleo board.
I installed the 1.02 patch provided in this repository to add support for the STM32C0 family and was able to build my project.
However, I was not able to use the IAR debugger after installing the patch : IAR reported an error "Failed to load flash loader <...>/FlashSTM32C03xx6.flash" :

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16e24021-8684-49f5-92d1-e1a508942d2b)

The IAR debug log indicated that the script STM32C0xx.dmac failed to run at line 96 in the enable_dbg_clock() function :

  rcc_apbenr1_restore = __readMemory32(0x4002103C, "AP0_Memory");


After some trial and error, I stumbled upon the IAR C-SPY Debugging Guide mentioning the prototype of this function :

__readMemory32(address, zone)

This document also states that the only zone available in ARM architecture is "Memory".
I replaced all the occurrences of "AP0_Memory" by the string "Memory" in the STM32C0xx.dmac script, and everything works fine now.

I don't know if this issue is specific to my version of IAR (8.32) but if this patch is compatible with all 8.x versions, it could be upstreamed to avoid uneccessary trouble for other developers :)

Title: SRAM_SIZE_MAX in stm32c011xx.h is wrong

Body:
Hi there!

See:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeC0/blob/main/Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32C0xx/Include/stm32c011xx.h#L501C1-L501C89

#define SRAM_SIZE_MAX         (0x00001500UL)  /*!< maximum SRAM size (up to 6 KBytes) */

Please correct me if I'm wrong :) The comment is correct. The SRAM size is 6k but the HEX value is wrong. It must be 0x00001800UL

Regards,
Pieter
https://piconomix.com
